p01.label: Te'kula village

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, so, short intro: as you are leaving the village of, of the Te'kula, following Theba and your friends back to the material world, keenly aware of the tanshi that seemed to hover just beyond your senses.

p01.note: Neshet identifies the Te'kula village in its canonical note; the opening occurs while leaving its pocket-dimensional refuge.

p02.label: Path out of the collapsing pocket dimension

evidence.quote:
DM: You can almost feel the hand of Aasimti holding this place hidden in light and shadow. The path seems to splinter and shift, as if seen through blinking, broken glass, and you sense the work of Birich'iko, the spirit of glass, in your vision. You feel rain on your face, the water soaking into the ground, and for a moment you sense the presence of Ch'ik'a as you almost feel the squashing of mud on your bare feet, through your armored boots.

DM: As you walk, distracted by your newfound awareness of the spirits that flit around you, suddenly your—when your vision is pulled back to your friends in a jumbled collection of images, as the pocket dimension collapses: a ship approaching a jagged coastline of an unfamiliar island, a meadow of golden butterflies, a dense tropical forest. As you feel Kenzo, Wellby and Seeker pulled away from you, you hear Wellby's voice in your mind just for a moment: "Find your way to the Feywild, to the portal near Eudomes' Tower; we will meet again there." And then you are hurtling towards the ground.

p03.label: Northern mountains

evidence.quote: DM: It is late afternoon trending towards dusk, and you see below you the slopes of tall mountains, the peaks tipped in white, dense fir-pine forests covering the slopes. There's a chill in the air, the hint of a long winter to come. Stretching to the west, rugged hills of mixed forest, the maples of the lower elevations already turning vibrant reds and yellows. The sun low in the sky casts a beautiful golden light across the forest and mountains. In the distance in the valleys, you see a hint of shadows, dark spots, with no obvious clouds drifting over the ground. In the next moment you find yourself on the ground in the pine forests about halfway up the mountains, watching the light of a flickering campfire in the evening a few hundred feet ahead of you.

DM: Yeah, everything there, Ainumarya's to the south. A fair bit to the south, they are, and as you know, they, they—somebody draws like a crude map, just the mountain, the central mountains, and then draws the little chain of volcanoes that is Pandar, and you are like 200 miles south of Pandar. You're like way to the north.

DM: Um, and this used to be like pretty—this used to be like the center of Deno'qai civilization north of the elves, like 400, 500 years ago, until Cha'mutte moved in and wiped everything out. So you got that sort of story from this young boy Zevi who's guiding you.

DM: And when you arrive, you know, a couple days after landing in the village, it's reminiscent in a lot of ways of the Deno'qai villages in the wood, it's the—there's the village clearing, there's like the tanshi tree and an altar, there's a big fire pit there, but the—it's, you know, everything's A-frames with like log—insulated log cabins and thatch roofs that go down to the ground. There's no pigs around, there's no chickens, there's no farm. There's some reindeer. But, you know, it's very, it's, it's clear you've gotten both far north and even in the two-day journey up several thousand feet, right, so you've gotten from maybe 2,000 to like five or 6,000. You're getting up to a decent elevation, all pines at this place.

p03.note: Northern Sentinels resolves the far-northern mountain setting through the Ko'zula and the campaign record.

p05.label: First hunting camp

evidence.quote:
DM: So, as you approach, you can almost sense what you will see before you see it. This is a hunting camp: about a dozen people carrying on the work of preparing the camp for the night. There's tents, fur blankets, several large elk and deer being butchered. Some already butchered, their skins salted, deer hides stretched between trees drying, a charcoal pit smoking as meat is dried for jerky.

DM: As you approach, perhaps somewhat disoriented, you hear, you know, some whistles, some obvious calls of the watchers, the lookouts at the camp, and four or five of the people begin gathering bows and shields and heading towards the—sort of peering into the gloom of the shadows, looking at you, and one calls in Deno'qai, which, at this point, I'm going to say you've now learned to—

DM: They, they sort of move to surround you slightly and motion you forward into the sort of light of the, of the fire, and the man who's speaking, is calling out to you, is—

Delwath: I'll reply in Deno'qai.

markers.reading: The table revisits the first camp before departure for geographic questions and campfire stories.

evidence.quote:
Delwath: Before we leave camp, actually, does any of them have any geographic sense? Like has any of them traveled far enough to have any way of sort of positioning us? Like how far north, like even which direction we are from Ainu—

DM: Yeah, everything there, Ainumarya's to the south. A fair bit to the south, they are, and as you know, they, they—somebody draws like a crude map, just the mountain, the central mountains, and then draws the little chain of volcanoes that is Pandar, and you are like 200 miles south of Pandar. You're like way to the north.

Delwath: I want to—I mean, at some point, maybe in the night, but—or maybe just this guy—Delwath will express some curiosity and stories of how they survived the Great War. They must have myths and legends.

DM: Oh yeah, so yeah, he tells you they—so most of them did, and there were once many tribes, the only one that survived—the only two tribes that survived the Great War were, were there's the Ko'zula and the Shu'anra who live further to the south.

DM: And, and tells you like, you know, "Ninu knows the legends, she'll tell you more, but there were many great battles and silent ones sacrificed themselves for our safety. And we fled into the mountains and fled to the protection of the stoneborn and lived in the high peaks for a generation sheltered by—in stoneborn refuges." You know, the myth anyway is they only escaped because the six silent ones sacrificed to delay Cha'mutte's troops long enough.

Delwath: I will recount the tale of Yezali, but from like a first person perspective, right, way—right, I mean I feel like I'm not going to dig it up, but there was a fairly detailed description in the dream, so like—

Delwath: Yes, maybe around the campfire, like if the story is coming out right now, Delwath will just take the opportunity to sort of share, and, and pitch it as kind of like, not he was there, but "I saw this through Yezali's eyes."

DM: So they, I mean they recognize some part of fighting the giant demon is like that's the Battle of Darkfire, that's a huge, like a major—right, legend, that Yezali sacrificed himself, themselves, with them during the Battle of Darkfire to prevent the forest from burning entirely.
